paper.title: Benchmarking Autonomy: A Taxonomy of Human-in-the-Loop Checkpoints for AI-Generated Transformation Code
paper.venue: International Journal of Computational and Experimental Science and Engineering

summary.text: A benchmark and taxonomy for human review of AI-generated data transformations. The premise is that generated SQL, Spark and dbt code can compile, run and preserve the expected schema while silently changing what downstream data means. Across 12 transformation tasks, nine with seeded defects, the authors evaluate three automated checkpoint families: schema checks and data-quality rules each catch one of nine defects, while comparison against a trusted baseline catches seven, and all combined catch eight. The one residual defect preserves schema, distributions, row counts and tolerance-bounded aggregates, and is found only by reviewing logic and business intent together.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Argues that semantic oracles outperform structural checks for silently wrong results, the same premise as SQLancer's oracles.
supporting_excerpts: A transformation may compile, complete successfully, and preserve an expected schema while silently changing the meaning of downstream data.
First, validation depth matters more than check quantity: semantic oracles materially outperform purely structural controls.
